points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 歌德出生于法兰克福一个富裕的中产阶级家庭。从小接受良好教育，在家人的指导下学习多种语言，包括拉丁语、法语、英语和意大利语。16岁时进入莱比锡大学学习法律，但更热衷于文学和艺术创作。这一时期他开始写作诗歌和戏剧，受到启蒙运动思想影响，形成了早期的文学风格。法兰克福的童年和青年时期为歌德日后的创作奠定了基础，尤其是他对人性、自然和社会的深刻观察。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Frankfurt to a wealthy middle-class family, Goethe received an excellent education, learning multiple languages including Latin, French, English, and Italian under family guidance. At 16, he entered Leipzig University to study law but became more passionate about literature and artistic creation. During this period, he began writing poetry and plays, influenced by Enlightenment ideas, forming his early literary style. His childhood and youth in Frankfurt laid the foundation for his future works, particularly his profound observations on human nature, society, and the natural world.

points.title: 狂飙突进时期
points.description: 在斯特拉斯堡大学继续法律学习期间，歌德结识了赫尔德，这位思想家对民间文学和莎士比亚作品的推崇深刻影响了歌德。歌德开始狂飙突进运动，创作了戏剧《葛兹·冯·伯利欣根》和早期版本的《少年维特之烦恼》。这一时期他形成了对自然和情感的独特理解，强调个人情感和自由意志。斯特拉斯堡的经历标志着歌德从传统古典主义向浪漫主义过渡的关键阶段，他的创作开始展现对人性解放的渴望和对社会束缚的反抗。
points.descriptionEn: While continuing his legal studies at the University of Strasbourg, Goethe met Herder, whose advocacy of folk literature and Shakespeare profoundly influenced him. Goethe became associated with the Sturm und Drang movement, writing the play 'Götz von Berlichingen' and an early version of 'The Sorrows of Young Werther'. During this period, he developed his unique understanding of nature and emotion, emphasizing personal feelings and free will. His time in Strasbourg marked a crucial transition from traditional classicism to romanticism, with his works beginning to express a longing for human liberation and rebellion against social constraints.

points.title: 魏玛早期
points.description: 1775年，歌德应卡尔·奥古斯特公爵邀请前往魏玛，最初担任政治顾问，后担任枢密院顾问和财政部长。在魏玛初期，歌德积极参与政治改革，推动农业、矿业和基础设施建设，同时继续文学创作。这一时期他创作了《伊菲格尼在陶里斯》等戏剧作品，并开始研究自然科学，特别是植物学和光学。魏玛的政治生涯使歌德获得了丰富的社会经验，但也使他面临艺术创作与政治责任的平衡问题。1782年，歌德获得贵族头衔，成为约翰·沃尔夫冈·冯·歌德。
points.descriptionEn: In 1775, Goethe was invited to Weimar by Duke Carl August, initially serving as a political advisor and later as a Privy Councilor and Finance Minister. During his early Weimar years, he actively participated in political reforms, promoting agriculture, mining, and infrastructure development while continuing his literary work. He wrote plays like 'Iphigenia in Tauris' and began studying natural sciences, particularly botany and optics. His political career in Weimar provided him with rich social experience but also forced him to balance artistic creation with political responsibilities. In 1782, Goethe was ennobled, becoming Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.

points.title: 意大利之旅
points.description: 1786年，歌德以匿名方式前往意大利，游历了罗马、那不勒斯、西西里等地。这次旅行对歌德的艺术观和世界观产生了深远影响。他深入研究古典艺术和建筑，临摹大师作品，并重新审视自己的创作风格。在意大利期间，歌德完成了《埃格蒙特》和《托夸多·塔索》等戏剧，并开始构思《浮士德》第二部分。意大利之旅标志着歌德从狂飙突进向古典主义的转变，他的作品变得更加平衡、和谐，对古典形式的追求取代了早期的情感宣泄。这次旅行也使歌德重新思考艺术与自然的关系，形成了'自然与艺术和谐统一'的美学理念。
points.descriptionEn: In 1786, Goethe traveled to Italy anonymously, visiting Rome, Naples, Sicily, and other places. This journey profoundly influenced his artistic and philosophical outlook. He studied classical art and architecture intensively, copying masterworks and reevaluating his own creative style. During his Italian sojourn, he completed the plays 'Egmont' and 'Torquato Tasso' and began构思 the second part of 'Faust'. The Italian journey marked Goethe's transition from Sturm und Drang to classicism, with his works becoming more balanced and harmonious, as the pursuit of classical forms replaced his earlier emotional expression. This trip also led Goethe to reconsider the relationship between art and nature, forming his aesthetic principle of 'harmony between nature and art'.

points.title: 魏玛后期
points.description: 1794年，歌德与席勒开始密切合作，这一文学友谊持续至席勒去世。在魏玛后期，歌德创作了多部重要作品，包括《威廉·迈斯特的学习时代》、《浮士德》第一部和第二部分、《西东诗集》以及《亲和力》。他还完成了色彩理论和地质学研究。歌德在魏玛担任剧院总监，推动了魏玛文化繁荣。这一时期，歌德的思想更加成熟，作品融合了古典主义的严谨与浪漫主义的激情，形成了独特的'魏玛古典主义'风格。他与席勒的友谊成为德国文学史上最著名的文学友谊之一，两人互相启发，共同推动了德国文学的黄金时代。
points.descriptionEn: In 1794, Goethe began his close collaboration with Schiller, which lasted until Schiller's death. During his later Weimar years, Goethe created several major works, including 'Wilhelm Meister's Apprenticeship', both parts of 'Faust', 'West-Eastern Divan', and 'Elective Affinities'. He also completed his research on color theory and geology. As theater director in Weimar, Goethe promoted the city's cultural flourishing. During this period, Goethe's thought matured, and his works merged the rigor of classicism with the passion of romanticism, forming a unique 'Weimar Classicism' style. His friendship with Schiller became one of the most famous literary friendships in German literary history, with the two mutually inspiring and jointly advancing the golden age of German literature.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 歌德的晚年主要致力于整理和出版自己的作品，同时继续创作诗歌和散文。这一时期他完成了《浮士德》的第二部分，这部作品被视为德国文学的巅峰之作。歌德还研究了植物形态学，提出了'原型'概念，对后世生物学产生影响。在政治上，歌德经历了法国大革命和拿破仑战争，形成了保守的政治立场，但他始终保持着对知识的开放态度。歌德的晚年生活平静而充实，他成为欧洲知识界的中心人物，吸引了来自各地的学者和艺术家。1832年3月22日，歌德在魏玛逝世，享年83岁，被安葬在王侯公墓。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Goethe primarily focused on organizing and publishing his works while continuing to write poetry and prose. During this period, he completed the second part of 'Faust', considered the pinnacle of German literature. Goethe also studied plant morphology, proposing the concept of 'archetype' that influenced later biology. Politically, Goethe experienced the French Revolution and Napoleonic Wars, developing a conservative stance while maintaining an open attitude toward knowledge. His later life was peaceful and fulfilling, with Goethe becoming a central figure in European intellectual circles, attracting scholars and artists from around the world. On March 22, 1832, Goethe died in Weimar at the age of 83 and was buried in the Ducal Vault.

appraisal.zh: 歌德通常被视为德国最伟大的文学巨匠之一，其创作横跨诗歌、戏剧、小说与科学，以《浮士德》等作品探索人类对知识与永恒的追求，并以魏玛古典主义结合古典形式的完美与浪漫主义的激情，成为启蒙与浪漫主义之间的桥梁。不过也有研究者指出，他在魏玛任职期间推行保守政策，对社会变革态度谨慎，其色彩理论亦被讥为缺乏严格科学方法，这些时代烙印构成其历史局限。
appraisal.en: Goethe is generally regarded as one of Germany's greatest literary figures, whose work spans poetry, drama, fiction, and science; through works such as Faust he explored humanity's pursuit of knowledge and eternity, and as a representative of Weimar Classicism he fused classical perfection with romantic passion, bridging the Enlightenment and Romanticism. Yet some researchers note that his conservative policies as a Weimar official and his caution toward social change, along with a color theory faulted for lacking rigorous method, mark the limits imposed on him by his era.

supporter.zh: 歌德被视为德国最伟大的文学巨匠之一，他的作品跨越了诗歌、戏剧、小说和科学领域，展现了人类精神的丰富性。支持者认为歌德通过《浮士德》等作品探索了人类追求知识与永恒的永恒主题，他的自然哲学和色彩理论对后世科学和艺术产生深远影响。歌德作为魏玛古典主义的代表，将古典形式的完美与浪漫主义的激情相结合，创造了独特的艺术风格。他的跨学科视野和对知识的全面追求使他成为启蒙时代与浪漫主义之间的桥梁，影响了从爱因斯坦到托马斯·曼等后世思想家。
supporter.en: Goethe is regarded as one of Germany's greatest literary giants, whose works span poetry, drama, fiction, and science, demonstrating the richness of the human spirit. Supporters believe that through works like 'Faust', Goethe explored humanity's eternal quest for knowledge and eternity, and his natural philosophy and color theory profoundly influenced later science and art. As a representative of Weimar Classicism, Goeth combined the perfection of classical forms with the passion of romanticism, creating a unique artistic style. His interdisciplinary vision and comprehensive pursuit of knowledge made him a bridge between the Enlightenment and Romanticism, influencing later thinkers from Einstein to Thomas Mann.

critic.zh: 批评者指出歌德的政治立场存在矛盾，他在魏玛担任政府官员期间推行保守政策，与法国大革命后的自由主义思潮形成鲜明对比。歌德对贵族制度的忠诚和对社会变革的谨慎态度被一些人视为妥协和保守。此外，歌德在《浮士德》中对玛格丽特的描写被批评为带有性别偏见，反映了当时社会对女性的刻板印象。一些现代评论家还认为歌德的科学理论，尤其是色彩理论，缺乏严格的科学方法，更接近哲学思辨而非真正的科学探索。这些批评反映了歌德作为历史人物的局限性，以及他思想中的时代烙印。
critic.en: Critics point out contradictions in Goethe's political stance. While serving as a government official in Weimar, he implemented conservative policies, contrasting sharply with the liberal思潮 after the French Revolution. Goethe's loyalty to the aristocratic system and cautious attitude toward social change are seen by some as compromises and conservatism. Additionally, his portrayal of Margaret in 'Faust' has been criticized for gender bias, reflecting contemporary societal stereotypes. Some modern commentators also argue that Goethe's scientific theories, particularly his color theory, lacked rigorous scientific methods, leaning more toward philosophical speculation than genuine scientific inquiry. These criticisms reflect the limitations of Goethe as a historical figure and the imprints of his era on his thought.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，歌德被定义为德国文化的象征和世界文学的重要人物。他的作品被广泛翻译和研究，成为全球文学经典。歌德的《浮士德》被视为西方文学中最伟大的作品之一，其主人公浮士德成为人类不断追求知识和超越的象征。在流行文化中，歌德的形象超越了单纯的文学巨匠，成为知识、智慧和人文精神的代表。他的名言'人不能两次踏入同一条河流'被广泛引用，体现了他的动态世界观。歌德的思想对德国民族认同的形成产生了深远影响，他的名字与魏玛一起成为德国文化黄金时代的象征，至今仍影响着文学、哲学、科学和艺术领域。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Goethe is defined as a symbol of German culture and a significant figure in world literature. His works have been widely translated and studied, becoming global literary classics. 'Faust' is regarded as one of the greatest works in Western literature, with its protagonist becoming a symbol of humanity's continuous pursuit of knowledge and transcendence. In popular culture, Goethe's image transcends that of a mere literary giant, representing knowledge, wisdom, and humanistic spirit. His famous quote 'One cannot step twice into the same river' is widely cited, reflecting his dynamic worldview. Goethe's thought profoundly influenced the formation of German national identity, and his name, along with Weimar, has become a symbol of Germany's cultural golden age, continuing to influence literature, philosophy, science, and art to this day.

self.zh: 人不能两次踏入同一条河流。
self.en: One cannot step twice into the same river.
